correctness.rationale: After a common phase and permutation, any torus triple has first two phases e^{±iθ} with 0<=θ<=π/2. Writing u=cosθ, x=u², v=cosφ and A=4x-s-2<0, expansion gives |P_s|²=(A-1)²+4s²u²+4Av²-4su(A+1)v. Completing the square in v and factoring H_s-G_s(x) gives exactly the stated two nonnegative terms for every s>2 and all torus phases. Independent exact symbolic cancellation returned identically zero. For s in [(1+sqrt(17))/2,4], x=1 with v=s(3-s)/(2(2-s)) in [-1,1] attains H_s. The alternate zero branch x=(s²-s-4)/(4(s-2)), whenever feasible, forces v*=u and hence two equal coordinates; permutation reduces it to x=1. Thus all maximizing triples are those stated modulo common phase and permutation; endpoint coincidences are included. Preexisting sharp Schur-Agler ratio is not re-claimed.

value.rationale: The Kaijser–Varopoulos/Holbrook three-variable quadratic is a standard sharp test for the Schur–Agler norm gap. An exact nonnegative two-term pointwise phase deficit and complete extremizing torus orbit classify equality beyond the known ratio, and provide an explicit quantitative stability witness. This is mathematically useful as an equality-geometry refinement, even though it does not produce a new norm-ratio bound.
